ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: actual 10.0 km minus optimal 8.5 km is 1.50 km, which exceeds POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so this is not a within-tolerance trip and a refund is on the table rather than closed off. I rely on the recorded distances, not on the GPS trace, because POL-RD-22 directs that the trace is not used to re-measure distance.

The driver-device trace independently shows the route taken was Woodlands Square, Woodlands Avenue 2, Woodlands Road, Bukit Panjang Road and Petir Road, with no fixes on the recommended Bukit Timah Expressway between the 15:51:59 deviation and the 16:03:01 rejoin; the artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the record of which route was taken is clean.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING - it carries no payload, its admissibility status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, so under POL-GEN-02 it carries no fact - and POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended route and overlapping the trip window. The driver's assertion of an accident on the BKE, with no such data, does not justify the reroute. I cite the absent artifact's id deliberately: its absence is the rider's point.

Because the deviation is over 1.0 km and the reroute is not traffic-justified, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies and only that row: the excess distance fare is refunded in full, being the deviation distance times the per-km rate, 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.08 SGD, without surge, rounded to the cent. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.08 SGD and it is the remedy this clause provides.

Nothing has already been returned to the rider: the fare ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0 and refund_already_issued_sgd 0.0, so the 1.08 SGD the matrix awards is still outstanding in full and the present state is not one in which the disputed distance has been paid back.

The driver's in-app message at 15:49:39 and the rider's 'ok can' at 15:49:59 do not move this case into POL-RD-24 row (a), because row (a) requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as notified and agreed, and the traffic limb fails; under POL-RD-21 the chat log only settles that the rider was informed and acknowledged, not that the extra distance was excused. The rider's 'ok' was given on the driver's assertion of a BKE accident that no traffic data in this record supports.

There is no escalation on these facts. POL-RD-24's residual limb is for a case that fits no row, such as informed but objecting; this case fits row (d) exactly. On value, the contested 3.50 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band so an AI ruling is final at any confidence, both profiles carry fraud_flags 0 so no 0.95 threshold applies, and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not applied and would in any event be satisfied at 1.50 km.

I do not press the rider's full 3.50 SGD. The rider's claim is measured against the metered total of 14.05 SGD, but POL-RD-24 caps a route-deviation remedy at the excess distance fare, which here is 1.08 SGD, and I will not ask for a remedy the clause does not give. The rider's entitlement on this record is 1.08 SGD, and the contested balance above that figure is not payable under this policy.

The driver did exactly what POL-RD-21 requires. He told the rider of the reroute by in-app chat at 15:49:39 — 'Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' — which is more than two minutes before the platform logged the deviation from the BKE slip road at 15:51:59, so notice was given before the point of deviation as the clause demands. The rider answered 'ok can' at 15:49:59, and the chat log is precisely the artifact the clause names: where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, POL-RD-21 says the deviation is agreed. This was an announced and accepted reroute, not a concealed detour, and the rider's present claim is inconsistent with his own contemporaneous assent. EV-CHAT-05009 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The route the driver drove is the route he announced. The GPS trace and the platform trip record agree: the vehicle left the recommended route at Woodlands Avenue 2 / the BKE slip road, took Woodlands Road, and rejoined at Petir Road / Bukit Panjang Road, with recorded distances of 10.0 km actual against 8.5 km recommended — a 1.50 km deviation measured the POL-RD-22 way, from the platform's recorded distances. Nothing was hidden from the rider: he was told the reason and the road before the turn, and he approved it in the chat. The rider is now objecting to a route he authorised at the time.

The one limb of POL-RD-24 that this record cannot settle is traffic justification, and it cannot settle it because the artifact that would carry it is absent: EV-ADVIS-05009-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — the platform's request to the LTA feed timed out and was never retried. POL-GEN-26 names that exact fact ('whether traffic justified the reroute') and requires escalation where the evidence that would carry it is missing or impaired; POL-GEN-02 confirms a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and the prepass itself states the file is silent on traffic and that this silence 'is not a finding of no traffic'. POL-RD-23 addresses a driver's assertion against available data; here no traffic data was ever retrieved, so the question is unresolved rather than answered, and the driver should not lose on the platform's own failed feed. The case should be escalated, which holds the 14.05 SGD charge as it stands instead of refunding it, with the open question put to the reviewer: was the recommended BKE route congested or blocked at 15:51-16:03 on 2026-08-23?

The rider's ground of complaint is not evidence in this file. He says he 'could not find any accident news after' the trip — a later search that found nothing is not proof that the recommended BKE route was clear at 15:51 that day, and POL-GEN-25 requires a claim to rest on a cited artifact. Against that, the driver's account is contemporaneous and is corroborated by the chat log: he gave the rider both the reason and the alternative road at 15:49:39, before the deviation, and the rider accepted it at 15:49:59. The rider has produced no artifact that contradicts the driver's contemporaneous notice.

ruling.explanation:
This case goes to a human reviewer. No money moves: the 14.05 SGD already charged stays charged (held) and nothing is refunded, because the ruling does not stand on the record as it is.

What the record settles. The trip was a metered ride from Causeway Point to Hillion Mall. The platform's recorded distances are 8.5 km recommended and 10.0 km actual, a deviation of 1.50 km (POL-RD-22), which is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so this is not a within-tolerance trip. The GPS trace agrees on the route taken — Woodlands Avenue 2, Woodlands Road, Bukit Panjang Road, Petir Road, off the BKE between 15:51:59 and 16:03:01. The driver also told the rider in the in-app chat at 15:49:39 ('Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?'), before the deviation was logged at 15:51:59, and the rider answered 'ok can' at 15:49:59. POL-RD-21 is satisfied: notice was given before the point of deviation and the chat log records the rider's acknowledgement.

What the record cannot settle. The refund matrix in POL-RD-24 turns on whether the reroute was traffic-justified, and POL-RD-23 requires a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY covering the recommended BKE route in the trip window to show it. The only such artifact, EV-ADVIS-05009-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — the platform's request to the LTA traffic feed timed out and was not retried. It carries no fact (POL-GEN-02), so the file is silent on the BKE at that time; that silence is not a finding that the BKE was clear, and it is equally not a finding that it was blocked. The traffic limb is therefore undecided, the case fits no row of POL-RD-24, and POL-GEN-26 names this exact fact ('whether traffic justified the reroute') as one that escalates where the evidence that would carry it is missing. That is why this is an ESCALATE rather than a refund.

For the rider: the 3.50 SGD you ask for is not payable on any view of this record. POL-RD-24 caps a route-deviation remedy at the excess distance fare — 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, without surge — so the whole fare is never returned on these facts, and today even that 1.08 SGD cannot be paid, because the traffic limb is unresolved rather than failed. Arguing that the absent advisory 'proves' no justification would be reading an outcome off missing evidence, which POL-GEN-26 forbids.

For the driver: your account of an accident on the BKE cannot be confirmed from this record. POL-RD-23 needs traffic data, and a bare assertion of traffic does not justify a reroute. Your reroute was properly announced and accepted, which counts in your favour on POL-RD-21, but it does not by itself excuse the extra distance; only a positive traffic justification would take the case into row (a) and close it with no refund.

Open question for the reviewer: was the recommended BKE route congested, blocked or the site of an accident between 15:51 and 16:03 on 2026-08-23, and why did the LTA traffic-feed request fail and go unretried? Once that is answered the case resolves into POL-RD-24 row (a) (no refund) or row (d) (refund of the 1.08 SGD excess distance fare), with the 14.05 SGD charged standing in the meantime. Confidence is set at 0.70, below POL-RD-25's 0.80 for a route deviation; note that the contested value of 3.50 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so value alone would not send this case up — POL-GEN-26 does.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
